subject: Communication
title: Expatriate Failure: Why Assignments Go Wrong
description: A micro-lesson that makes Expatriate Failure: Why Assignments Go Wrong usable.

hook.text: 40% of international assignments fail — costing companies $250,000-$1 million per failure. The #1 reason isn't skills.

buildup.text: Companies select expatriates for technical competence, then wonder why they fail. The answer is almost never skills.

discovery.text: The biggest predictor of expatriate success isn't IQ or experience — it's cultural adaptability and openness.

twist.text: Family adjustment matters more than the employee's. If the spouse or children can't adapt, the assignment fails.

climax.text: Companies that invest in cultural training before assignments see failure rates drop from 40% to under 10%.

punchline.text: You can move people across borders. Moving them across cultures takes intention.

quiz.question: What is the biggest predictor of expatriate assignment success?

details.summary: Between 25 and 40 percent of international assignments fail, costing companies hundreds of thousands of dollars each. The primary failure reason is not technical incompetence but cultural adjustment problems for the employee and their family. Selection and preparation are crucial.
details.whyItMatters: Expatriate failure is one of the most expensive and avoidable costs in international business, driven almost entirely by cultural readiness gaps.
takeaways: 25 to 40 percent of expatriate assignments fail prematurely
Cultural adjustment, not technical skill, is the top failure cause
Family adaptation problems are the most common specific reason

faq.question: How can companies reduce expatriate failure rates?
faq.answer: Select for cultural intelligence and adaptability, not just technical skill. Provide pre-departure cultural training for the employee and family. Assign a mentor in the host country. Check in regularly during the first six months and provide adjustment support.

faq.question: Why is family adjustment so important to expatriate success?
faq.answer: A struggling spouse or unhappy children create constant pressure to return home. The employee cannot focus on work while the family is in crisis. Companies that provide spouse career support, school assistance, and community connections see dramatically better retention.
